reasoning_traces.think:
Split conformal prediction ensures validity by splitting data into calibration and test sets, where the former is used to compute conformity scores. These scores define prediction regions that maintain coverage guarantees under exchangeability. In contrast, conformalized quantile regression (CQR) extends this to regression tasks by predicting quantiles and adjusting intervals accordingly. Both methods rely on exchangeability as a foundational assumption. Failure occurs when data violates exchangeability, leading to invalid intervals. The key duality lies between the fixed model outputs in split conformal and the learned quantile functions in CQR. The breakdown regime manifests as overconfidence or undercoverage when assumptions fail. For GSE, these primitives enable adaptive interval estimation through state transitions driven by empirical coverage metrics.
